documents.source_title: UN SDG 12: Circular Economy Strategies for ICT Equipment
documents.author: United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) / ITU
documents.excerpt: Up to 80% of a computer's total lifecycle carbon emissions are emitted during the manufacturing, raw material extraction, and semiconductor fabrication phases. Extending active operational life from 3 years to 6 years through modular repair, refurbishment, or second-life repurposing reduces annualized carbon footprint by approximately 45% and conserves critical rare earth metals.

documents.source_title: Repurposing Decommissioned Hardware for Campus Infrastructure
documents.author: Open Source Campus Lab Consortium
documents.excerpt: Retired desktop towers and laptops with broken displays or degraded batteries are ideal for Linux-based headless servers, HomeAssistant lab automation, DNS sinkholes (Pi-hole), local network caching proxies, and Docker microservice runners. Repurposing achieves maximum hardware utilization with zero procurement overhead.
